title: Articles and store questions
explanation: At the grocery store you name things with a, an, or the, and you ask for help with Can I have...? and Where is...?

sections.heading: a, an, the
sections.text: Use a before a consonant sound (a bag, a cart, a loaf). Use an before a vowel sound (an apple, an aisle announcement). Use the when both of you know which one (the dairy aisle, the cashier, the flyer).

sections.heading: Can I have...? / Where is...?
sections.text: Can I have a bag? is a polite request at checkout. Where is the rice? or Where is aisle 4? asks for a place. Short answers are fine: Aisle 4, next to the dairy.

sections.heading: Count vs. uncount
sections.text: Count nouns take a number or a/an: a loaf, two bags, three apples. Uncount nouns do not: milk, rice, bread. Say some milk, a bag of rice, a loaf of bread — not a milk or two breads.

examples.note: apple starts with a vowel sound

examples.prompt: I bought some milk, not two milks.

try_it: At the store, say: Where is the dairy aisle? Can I have a bag?
